name: Eritrean Zigni
description: Zigni, meat slow-simmered in a deep berbere sauce, is widely considered Eritrea's national dish, closely related to Ethiopian doro wat given the countries' shared culinary heritage - real berbere, not a generic chili powder, is what gives it its actual identity.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion alone in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 12-15 minutes, until deeply softened.
Add the ghee and garlic, cooking 1 minute, then stir in the berbere and cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the beef and a splash of water, and simmer 20-22 minutes until the sauce is deep red and thick.

name: Eritrean Injera-Style Flatbread
description: Injera, a spongy, slightly sour flatbread made from fermented teff, is central to Eritrean eating just as it is in Ethiopia - a full days-long ferment is what gives real injera its distinctive tang, which this quicker version can only approximate.
steps_detailed: Whisk the teff flour, all-purpose flour, vinegar, and 1 cup water into a thin, smooth batter.
Let sit at room temperature at least 6-8 hours to develop some tang.
Pour a thin layer into a hot, lightly oiled non-stick pan and cook, covered, without flipping, 2-3 minutes, until bubbles cover the surface.

name: Eritrean Tsebhi Birsen
description: Tsebhi birsen, red lentils simmered in a berbere-spiced sauce, a genuine Eritrean staple, especially common during fasting periods.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat, 8-9 minutes, until softened.
Add the garlic and berbere, cooking 1-2 minutes.
Add the lentils and 1.5 cups water, and simmer 20-22 minutes until tender.

name: Eritrean Tsebhi Dorho
description: Tsebhi dorho, chicken slow-simmered in berbere sauce with a hard-boiled egg, is a beloved Eritrean celebration dish, closely related to Ethiopian doro wat.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion alone 12-15 minutes until deeply softened.
Add the ghee and berbere, cooking 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and a splash of water, and simmer 30-35 minutes until very tender.
Add the whole hard-boiled egg in the last 10 minutes to absorb the sauce.

name: Eritrean Tihlo
description: Tihlo, roasted barley flour dumplings dipped in a spiced meat sauce, a genuine Eritrean specialty from the country's highlands.
steps_detailed: Toast the flour in a dry pan until lightly golden and fragrant, 3-4 minutes.
Mix with hot water into a firm dough and shape into small dumplings.
Brown the beef with the berbere, 8-9 minutes, adding a splash of water to make a dipping sauce.
Serve the dumplings alongside the sauce for dipping.

name: Eritrean Ful
description: Ful, mashed fava beans with berbere and a fried egg, reflects genuine shared culinary threads between Eritrea and its northern neighbors.
steps_detailed: Simmer the fava beans with a splash of water 8-10 minutes, then mash roughly and stir in the berbere.
Fry the egg and serve on top.

name: Eritrean Shiro
description: Shiro, a smooth, spiced chickpea flour stew, is one of Eritrea's most common everyday dishes.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil, 6-7 minutes, then add the garlic and berbere, cooking 1 minute.
Whisk the chickpea flour with 1.5 cups water until smooth, then stir into the pot.
Simmer, stirring often, 10-12 minutes, until thickened and smooth.
